default.$description: The page ground. This system stays on white; there is no dark mode.

surface.$description: Lavender mist. Raised surfaces that sit on the ground: cards, inputs, dialogs.

section.$description: Section lavender. Tints a whole region or slide, never a card. Supports the brand's one-tint-per-section rule.

feature.$description: A full-bleed indigo panel. Use white text on it (7.00:1).

celebrate.$description: A full-bleed lime panel, reserved for genuine celebration. Use default text on it (12.32:1).

neutral.$description: Fond neutre teinté : une barre d’onglets, un panneau. Ne remplace pas bg/surface.

control.$description: Le fond d’un contrôle coché ou actif : case, radio, interrupteur allumé, chip sélectionné, ligne choisie d’une liste. Même valeur que le bouton principal, mais une variable à part pour que changer l’un ne déplace pas l’autre.

control-hover.$description: Le fond d’un contrôle coché ou actif, survolé.

default.$description: Pale lavender hairline, never grey. Aliases color/accent/100 since 27/08, when it was darkened so a chip could be seen at all: with no border, an unselected chip on the page ground was literally invisible. Decorative only at 1.44:1 on white — never let a border be the sole separator between two pieces of content. It does not reach the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks of the visible boundary of a control; in this ramp only accent/300 does (3.23:1), at the price of a far more present indigo on all 33 places that read this variable.

strong.$description: The heavier rule used to frame a photograph.

focus.$description: The keyboard focus ring. 7.00:1 on the ground, well past the 3:1 asked of UI boundaries.

focus-on-accent.$description: Anneau de focus sur un fond indigo.

control.$description: Le contour visible d’un champ, d’une case ou d’un chip. 3:1 minimum sur le sol, la surface et la section (4,66 / 4,15 / 3,72).

accent.$description: Liseré d’accent : le contour d’un tag.

hover.$description: Bordure d’un champ survolé. Décorative : 2,41:1 sur le sol.

default.$description: Warm near-black, never pure black. 13.67:1 on the ground.

muted.$description: The one quiet text step. 5.56:1 on the ground, 4.96:1 on surface. On section lavender it is 4.45:1 — large text only there.

accent.$description: Accent text: links, eyebrows, numerals. Safe at body size (7.00:1 on the ground).

on-accent-soft.$description: Secondary text on an indigo fill. 4.86:1 — passes, but leave it for supporting copy.

disabled.$description: Texte d’un élément inactif. 2,41:1, exempté : jamais pour du contenu.

on-danger.$description: Texte sur un fond de danger.

on-success.$description: Texte sur un fond de succès.

accent-hover.$description: Texte d’accent survolé. 8,24:1 sur le sol.

secondary.$description: Texte courant dense : le corps d’un dialogue. 9,10:1 sur le sol. Entre text/default et text/muted.

bg.$description: Fond du bouton principal au repos.

solid.$description: Couleur forte de l’action hors du bouton : icône, pastille, barre.

bg.$description: Fond du bouton secondaire au repos.

solid.$description: Couleur forte de l’action hors du bouton : icône, pastille, barre.

bg.$description: Fond du bouton d’alerte au repos.

solid.$description: Couleur forte de l’action hors du bouton : icône, pastille, barre.

bg-hover.$description: Lavis de survol d’une ligne, d’une case, d’une pastille : l’action sans fond au repos.

bg-pressed.$description: Lavis d’appui de l’action sans fond au repos : le bouton Ghost pressé.

bg-off.$description: Piste d’un interrupteur éteint. 5,56:1 sur le sol : passe le 3:1 des éléments d’interface (WCAG 1.4.11). Le pouce blanc s’y détache à 5,56:1.

text.$description: Texte sur la teinte pâle et sur le sol.
Texte sur la teinte pâle et sur le sol.
Texte sur la teinte pâle et sur le sol.

solid.$description: Pastille, icône, remplissage fort. Pas du texte courant : 3,02:1 sur le sol.

text.$description: Texte sur la teinte pâle et sur le sol.

solid.$description: Pastille, icône, astérisque, texte court : le rouge plein. 4,83:1 sur le sol.

bg.$description: Fond de tag ou de mémo.

solid.$description: Pastille, icône, remplissage fort de la catégorie.

bg.$description: Fond de tag ou de mémo.

solid.$description: Pastille, icône, remplissage fort de la catégorie.

xs.$description: The gap inside a small control.

sm.$description: Button padding, the gap between stacked labels, table cell padding.

md.$description: Card padding and the default gap between related items. The most-used step in the system.

lg.$description: Dialog padding, the gap between groups, the space above and below a rule.

xl.$description: The gap between blocks on a page.

2xl.$description: The gap between sections. The largest step used inside a component.

64.$description: Slide padding. The top and bottom margin of a 16:9 slide.

96.$description: A generous section break, or the left margin of a title slide.

128.$description: The largest step. Full-bleed breathing room.

sm.$description: Small chrome: a page-number badge, a code block, a swatch.

md.$description: The system's signature radius. Cards, inputs, dialogs — anything that holds content.

lg.$description: A roomy floating panel, and the frame around a photograph.

pill.$description: Fully round ends. Buttons, tags and segmented controls are always pills in this system.

heading.$description: Geometric sans, set at bold. Headings, buttons, brand marks. Free from Google Fonts; already in the Google Slides font picker.

body.$description: Neo-grotesque. Body copy and everything in the interface. Free from Google Fonts.

bold.$description: Every heading. This system sets headings at bold and nothing lighter.

display.$description: H1, and the headline on a title slide.

title.$description: H2, and a section divider slide.

brand.$description: The wordmark in a header bar.

body-lg.$description: A lead paragraph, one notch above body.

ui.$description: Buttons, inputs, nav links, table cells. Deliberately one size so a button and a field sit level side by side.

body-sm.$description: Dense body copy, card body, and the H6 eyebrow. H6 and small body share this size — that is intentional, not a duplicate.

label.$description: Table headers, card metadata, figure captions. Anything at this size must use text.default or text.muted — nothing dimmer passes AA here.

micro.$description: The uppercase kicker on a card. The smallest size in the system.

tight.$description: Headings. Token value is the unitless multiplier 1.12; Figma states line height as a percentage, so it is stored here as 112%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives a line height in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

snug.$description: Buttons and card titles — text that sits on one or two lines. Token value is the unitless multiplier 1.2; Figma states line height as a percentage, so it is stored here as 120%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives a line height in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

body.$description: Body copy. Token value is the unitless multiplier 1.55; Figma states line height as a percentage, so it is stored here as 155%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives a line height in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

tight.$description: Headings. Large type needs pulling together. Token value is -0.015em; Figma states letter spacing as a percentage, so it is stored here as -1.5%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives letter spacing in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

normal.$description: Body copy and everything not listed here. Token value is 0em; Figma states letter spacing as a percentage, so it is stored here as 0%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives letter spacing in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

wide.$description: Tags. Token value is 0.02em; Figma states letter spacing as a percentage, so it is stored here as 2%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives letter spacing in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

wider.$description: The H6 eyebrow and table headers. Token value is 0.08em; Figma states letter spacing as a percentage, so it is stored here as 8%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives letter spacing in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

widest.$description: The card kicker, the smallest uppercase text in the system. Token value is 0.1em; Figma states letter spacing as a percentage, so it is stored here as 10%. Same value, different notation. ⚠️ DO NOT bind this variable to a text style. A number variable carries the number but not the unit, so Figma applies it as PIXELS — binding this gives letter spacing in px, not a percentage. Type the percentage into the style by hand, and keep this variable for the code, which converts it. Measured 27/08.

radius.$description: Button border radius. Aliases radius/pill for full-rounded buttons.

focus-offset.$description: Focus ring offset (3px). WCAG 2.4.13 — visible separation from button edge.

focus-ring-width.$description: Focus ring width (3px). Exceeds WCAG 2.4.13 minimum (2px) for maximum visibility.

target-spacing.$description: Minimum spacing between adjacent buttons (24px). WCAG 2.5.8 Target Spacing — ensures no accidental activation of neighboring targets.

sm.$description: Small button height (44px). Meets WCAG 2.5.5 AAA minimum touch target.

md.$description: Medium button height (48px). Meets Apple HIG & Material 3 recommended minimum.

lg.$description: Large button height (56px). Maximum comfort, exceeds all guidelines.

sm.$description: Small button horizontal padding (16px). Ensures text never crowds edges.

md.$description: Medium button horizontal padding (24px). Comfortable reading area.

lg.$description: Large button horizontal padding (32px). Maximum legibility.

sm.$description: Small button vertical padding (12px). Ensures 44px minimum height with text.

md.$description: Medium button vertical padding (16px). Comfortable for 48px height.

lg.$description: Large button vertical padding (24px). Maximum comfort for 56px height.

sm.$description: Small button icon-to-label gap (8px). Clear separation for cognitive accessibility.

md.$description: Medium/large button icon-to-label gap (12px). Generous spacing for clarity.

sm.$description: Small button icon (20px). Above WCAG minimum for perceivable graphics.

md.$description: Medium button icon (24px). Meets WCAG AAA for interactive graphic elements.

lg.$description: Large button icon (28px). Exceeds all guidelines for maximum visibility.

sm.$description: Small button minimum width (44px). WCAG 2.5.5 AAA in both dimensions.

md.$description: Medium button minimum width (96px). Ensures comfortable label space.

lg.$description: Large button minimum width (140px). Maximum legibility and tap confidence.

quick.$description: 140ms. Colour changes and fades — anything that does not travel: a hover fill, an opacity swap. Do NOT use it for movement; at this speed a path cannot be read.

default.$description: 200ms. Movement inside the screen: something that slides from one place to another while staying visible. The nav pill travels on this one.

slow.$description: 320ms. Things that enter or leave the screen — a dialog, a drawer. Not yet used: it waits for the contact dialog. Do NOT use it for a hover; it would feel broken.

standard.$description: An object that moves while staying on screen: it leaves briskly and settles. The default curve — reach for this one first, and pair it with duration.default.

enter.$description: Something arriving: full speed at the start, gentle landing. Pair with duration.slow. Only for what comes from outside the screen.

exit.$description: Something leaving: gentle start, then gone. Pair with duration.slow. Never on something that stays — it reads as a departure.

height.$description: The height of the nav bar when it sticks to the top: a tab, plus the air the pill puts around it, plus the air the bar puts around the pill. 88 above 768, 72 below. A page reads it to sit its first screen under the bar — it is the number the case study peek depends on. Same in both Nav states: the avatar is exactly as tall as the pill.

size.$description: Card title size. Aliases font/size/title — the same step an H2 takes. Named so the text of a card can be retuned without moving page headings.

color.$description: Card title ink. Aliases color/text/default. 15.3:1 on color/bg/default, which is what a card is painted with.

size.$description: Card subtitle size. Aliases font/size/body-lg — one step above body, so the line under the title reads before the secondary one.

color.$description: Card subtitle ink. Aliases color/text/default: the subtitle carries meaning, so it reads at full strength and is not muted.

size.$description: Card secondary info size. Aliases font/size/body — a date, a place, an author. Read after the subtitle, so it does not shrink below body.

color.$description: Card secondary info ink. Aliases color/text/muted. 5.56:1 on color/bg/default — the only quiet step, and it stays above 4.5:1 on the card.

size.$description: The side of a compact control's box — radio, checkbox. Both are drawn at 18.

track-height.$description: The height of a switch track. Its width needs no variable: 40 is space/xl + space/lg exactly.

field-gap.$description: The vertical gap between a field's label, its box and its counter. Not the gap between a compact control and its word — that one is space/sm.

height.$description: Hauteur d'un champ d'une ligne (Text field, Select, Multi Select, recherche de liste). Alignée sur button/height/sm — un champ et un bouton posés côte à côte tombent au même niveau. Le rembourrage vertical n'est pas appliqué : c'est la hauteur qui centre le texte.

default.$description: The resting stroke of a field, a box, a chip. The system's only one: drawn 217 times across five pages.

focus.$description: The focus mark. Every control that carries one draws it at 2. Supersedes button/focus-ring-width, which draws nothing — the Button has no Focused state.

disabled.$description: How far a disabled object fades, in percent — Figma stores opacity the way it stores line-height. One value for all of them, where the file had drawn 40, 50 and 60 for the same intent.

y.$description: Vertical offset. The contact layer, shared by every shadow in the system. It is also shadow/sm on its own — the faintest lift there is. Tinted with the text ink, never black.

blur.$description: Blur radius. The contact layer, shared by every shadow in the system. It is also shadow/sm on its own — the faintest lift there is. Tinted with the text ink, never black.

spread.$description: Spread. The contact layer, shared by every shadow in the system. It is also shadow/sm on its own — the faintest lift there is. Tinted with the text ink, never black.

color.$description: The contact layer, shared by every shadow in the system. It is also shadow/sm on its own — the faintest lift there is. Tinted with the text ink, never black. No shadow in this system has a horizontal offset, so none is named.

y.$description: Vertical offset. The bloom of the default card elevation. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/md.

blur.$description: Blur radius. The bloom of the default card elevation. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/md.

spread.$description: Spread. The bloom of the default card elevation. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/md.

color.$description: The bloom of the default card elevation. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/md. No shadow in this system has a horizontal offset, so none is named.

y.$description: Vertical offset. The bloom of the top elevation, for a dialog or a floating panel. The negative spread keeps it from creeping out sideways. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg.

blur.$description: Blur radius. The bloom of the top elevation, for a dialog or a floating panel. The negative spread keeps it from creeping out sideways. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg.

spread.$description: Spread. The bloom of the top elevation, for a dialog or a floating panel. The negative spread keeps it from creeping out sideways. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg.

color.$description: The bloom of the top elevation, for a dialog or a floating panel. The negative spread keeps it from creeping out sideways. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg. No shadow in this system has a horizontal offset, so none is named.

y.$description: Vertical offset. The same top elevation, thrown upwards — for a panel that rises over what it covers. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg-invert.

blur.$description: Blur radius. The same top elevation, thrown upwards — for a panel that rises over what it covers. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg-invert.

spread.$description: Spread. The same top elevation, thrown upwards — for a panel that rises over what it covers. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg-invert.

color.$description: The same top elevation, thrown upwards — for a panel that rises over what it covers. Composed with shadow/contact to make shadow/lg-invert. No shadow in this system has a horizontal offset, so none is named.
